{{Short description|Norwegian chemist (1932–2022)}}
'''Synnøve Liaaen Jensen''' (1 March 1932 – 22 April 2022) was a [[Norway|Norwegian]] chemist.

She took the {{ill|dr.techn.|no}} degree in 1963 as the first woman in Norway, and became the first female professor at the Norwegian Institute of Technology. She was a professor of [[theoretical chemistry]] there from 1970 to her retirement. She also received an [[honorary degree]] at the [[University of Zurich]]<ref>[http://www.archiv.uzh.ch/dam/jcr:ffffffff-92dc-1ae4-ffff-ffffd36d4e6f/Jahresbericht_UZH_1986_1987.pdf Universität Zürich Jahresbericht 1986 1987, S. 104]</ref> in 1986.<ref name=snl>{{cite encyclopedia|year=|title=Synnøve Liaaen Jensen|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|url=http://www.snl.no/Synnøve_Liaaen_Jensen|language=Norwegian|accessdate=19 December 2022}}</ref><ref name=nbl>{{cite encyclopedia|year=|title=Synnøve Liaaen Jensen|encyclopedia=[[Norsk biografisk leksikon]]|first=Arne Jørgen|last=Aasen|editor=[[Knut Helle|Helle, Knut]]|publisher=Kunnskapsforlaget|location=Oslo|url=http://www.snl.no/.nbl_biografi/Synnøve_Liaaen_Jensen/utdypning|language=Norwegian|accessdate=12 September 2012}}</ref> She was a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27627|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|title=Gruppe 4: Kjemi|language=Norwegian|accessdate=12 September 2012}}</ref> and the [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ntva.no/index.php?option=com_club&view=member&id=224%3Ajensen-synnove-inga-johanne-liaaen&Itemid=60|title=Medlemmer: JENSEN, Synnøve Inga Johanne Liaaen|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]]|language=Norwegian|accessdate=4 December 2012}}</ref>
